items.feedback: Correct. Your code runs the tool, which is why your code also controls permissions and errors.
Correct. Requests = tool calls + 1: three tool-use replies, then one more request to get the answer.
Correct. Each request is stateless, so the full history goes back every time, with the tool_result carrying the matching id.
Correct. Beyond cost and time, the cap also bounds a malformed tool that keeps the loop at tool_use.
Correct. Only tool_use continues the loop; end_turn means the text is the answer.

summary: 5 of 5 correct. You have the loop down: who runs tools, what each request carries, when it stops and why to cap it. Next step: ask for a lesson on workflows versus agents, or on writing a tool definition.
